note: Hand-authored. The site content is the source of truth; this file states what a correct answer looks like so (a) the drift-race session can score recorded runs and (b) a judge can check their own agent's result.

tasks.title: Needle in the haystack
tasks.difficulty: The rule is four clicks deep, in the middle of a 1,500-word FAQ, and the word 'waiver' never appears in the navigation.

persona.name: Mira Tanaka
persona.summary: Bakery owner in Zone 4, second claim this year.
persona.scenario: You are Mira Tanaka. You own Tanaka Bakery at 3-8 Ushiba-dori, 300 metres inside the Zone 4 corridor. Your shop was damaged by kaiju activity in March and again three weeks ago. The March claim was approved. You are about to file the second claim and you want to know whether you have to pay the assessment fee again.

tasks.prompt: Using this site, find out whether I have to pay the claim assessment fee a second time, and quote the rule.

expected.summary: No. Two or more approved claims from separate incidents in a rolling 12-month period exempt the claimant from the ¥12,000 assessment fee on subsequent claims in that period. It is applied automatically by the regional office.
expected.threshold: 2 approved claims from separate incidents in any rolling 12 months

checks.label: States the fee is waived / not payable again
Notes that no separate application is needed

tasks.title: Eligibility determination
tasks.shortTitle: Am I eligible, and what do I bring?
tasks.difficulty: The outcome depends on four separate rules spread across three pages, and two of them are conditional grants rather than the headline decision.

persona.name: Mira Tanaka
persona.summary: Zone 4 commercial property, structural damage, low household income, second claim.
persona.scenario: You are Mira Tanaka. Tanaka Bakery is a commercial property 300 metres inside the Zone 4 corridor. The incident was 21 days ago and caused verified structural damage to the shopfront and the rear wall. You have had two approved claims in the last 12 months, including this one. No insurer has paid out. Your annual household income is ¥3,600,000.

tasks.prompt: Using this site, tell me whether I am eligible for damage compensation, what extra support I qualify for, and exactly which documents I need to bring.

tasks.title: Permit prefill
tasks.difficulty: The reinforcement standard is never stated in the scenario — it has to be derived from the zone. The form is a real form, and the human presses submit.

persona.name: Mira Tanaka
persona.summary: Rebuilding the damaged shopfront; needs a proximity construction permit.
persona.scenario: You are Mira Tanaka, owner of Tanaka Bakery. You are rebuilding the damaged shopfront — a structural alteration, not a new building. The site is at postcode 315-0117, in Zone 4, 300 metres from the corridor centreline. The floor area is 96 m². Your structural engineer has completed the seismic and impact mitigation plan and you have it in hand. You want work to start on 1 October 2026. Contact details: mira@tanaka-bakery.example, 0299-55-0184.

tasks.prompt: Using this site, fill in my proximity construction permit application. Do not submit it — I will review and submit it myself.

derivedField.name: reinforcementStandard
derivedField.why: Not stated in the scenario. Zone 4 requires minimum standard K-2, per /permits/proximity/#standards.
